「に当（あ）たり」または「に当（あ）たって」は日本語（にほんご）の硬（かた）い文型（ぶんけい）で「(A) のときに」という意味（いみ）を表（あらわ）します。「に際（さい）して」と同様（どうよう）に、未来（みらい）の出来事（できごと）への準備（じゅんび）に関連（かんれん）して使（つか）われます。この文型（ぶんけい）は「に」と五段動詞（ごだんどうし）「当（あ）たる」のテ形（けい）または連用形（れんようけい）（丁寧（ていねい）な形（かたち））の組（く）み合（あ）わせでできています。

「に当（あ）たり」は動詞（どうし）の辞書形（じしょけい）または名詞（めいし）の後（あと）に付（つ）きます。この文型（ぶんけい）には主（おも）に二（ふた）つのニュアンスがあります。例（れい）をいくつか見（み）てみましょう！

一（ひと）つ目（め）は (A) が特別（とくべつ）な行事（ぎょうじ）や機会（きかい）であり、それに向（む）けて事前（じぜん）に (B) が行（おこな）われる場合（ばあい）です。

二（ふた）つ目（め）は (A) が目標（もくひょう）であり、それを実現（じつげん）するための手段（しゅだん）や対応（たいおう）が (B) である場合（ばあい）です。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「に際（さい）して」は肯定的（こうていてき）な場面（ばめん）にも否定的（ひていてき）な場面（ばめん）にも使（つか）えますが、「に当（あ）たり」は肯定的（こうていてき）または中立的（ちゅうりつてき）な場面（ばめん）で使（つか）われるのがふつうです。
attributes.body:
に当（あ）たり or に当（あ）たって is a formal grammar pattern in Japanese used to convey the meaning of 'at the time of (A)', 'when doing (A)', or 'on the occasion of (A)'. Like に際（さい）して 'on the occasion of (A)', it will often be used in regard to preparation for future events. This structure is a combination of に, and the う-Verb 当（あ）たる 'to hit', or 'to come into contact' in either its formal-conjunctive form or て-form.

に当（あ）たり will appear following verbs in their dictionary form, or nouns. There are two primary nuances that this structure will be used for, so let's look at a few examples of each.

The first is when (A) is some sort of special occasion or condition from which (B) will be done.

The second is when (A) is some sort of goal or target for which (B) will be the means or measures in response to that goal.

Caution

Unlike に際（さい）して, which can be used for either positive or negative situations, に当（あ）たり will primarily only be used for positive or neutral situations.

attributes.source: A Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Meaning of にあたって/にあたり

attributes.body: Both are formal expressions where one condition influences another, but with different nuance. につき means on account of or due to, as in 雨天につき中止になる (Cancelled due to rain). にあたり・にあたって means on the occasion of or at the time of, as in 退職にあたり一言挨拶をする (Say a few words on the occasion of retiring).

first_relatable.title: につき
first_relatable.meaning: Due to, On account of, Each or every

second_relatable.title: にあたり・にあたって
second_relatable.meaning: When, When doing something, On the occasion, At the time

attributes.body: Both mark the timing of an event. にあたり・にあたって emphasizes necessary preparations or intentions beforehand, as in 開発にあたり調査を行った (Before development, we conducted research). に際して marks the occasion itself, especially significant or ceremonial ones, as in 入学に際して祝辞を述べる (Give a congratulatory speech on the occasion of enrollment).

second_relatable.meaning: On the occasion of, At the time of

attributes.body: にあたり・にあたって is used for important occasions that involve preparation or intention, as in 出発にあたり挨拶をした (I gave a greeting on the occasion of departure). 際に simply means when or at the time of, describing something that happens concurrently, as in 出発の際に見送ってくれた (They saw me off at the time of departure).

second_relatable.title: 際に
second_relatable.meaning: When, At the time of, In case of, On the occasion of

attributes.body: Both derive from 当たる, but are used in different ways. に当たる means 'corresponds to' and functions as an indirect way of saying 'is', e.g. '父親に当たる人' ('a person who is [lit. corresponds to] their father'). にあたり・にあたって follows nouns or verb phrases and means 'when' or 'on the occasion of', e.g. '就職に当たり' ('on the occasion of getting a job'). Note that に当たる can also appear as に当たり in formal conjunctive form.

first_relatable.title: に当たる
first_relatable.meaning: Correspond to, Amounts to, Equals to, Is appropriate

second_relatable.title: にあたり・にあたって
second_relatable.meaning: When, When doing something, On the occasion, At the time

attributes.body: Both connect actions to a larger context, but with different emphasis. ついでに expresses performing a second action while it's convenient, e.g. '買い物のついでに郵便局に寄った' ('I stopped at the post office while shopping'). にあたり・にあたって is more formal and used for actions on a certain occasion, e.g. '開会にあたり、ご挨拶申し上げます' ('On the occasion of the opening, I extend my greetings').
